label: Run the trunk once, the denoiser many times
context: Left: a tall dark box 'trunk (Pairformer, 48–64 blocks)' with inputs 'sequence + MSA + templates' entering at the bottom; it runs once with a progress fill and a recycling arrow cycling 3–4 times, then emits a pill labelled 'c = (s, z)'. Right: a smaller box 'denoiser D_θ(x, σ | c)' with a loop arrow. Animate a 3D-ish point cloud structure (25 dots connected as a chain) starting as random noise; each loop iteration (a step counter going up to 200, sped up) the denoiser refines it, and a copy of c flows into the denoiser every step (warm dashed arrows). A small counter compares 'trunk calls: 1' versus 'denoiser calls: 200 × samples'. Then show 5 samples being produced in parallel from the same c. Canvas is responsive: width anywhere from 340 to 900 px, height 400 px; derive every size and position from width and height, keep all text at least 11 px and fully inside the canvas, and on narrow widths stack or shrink rather than overlap. Loop forever on a cycle of 10 to 16 s with smooth easing between phases. White background. Put a one-line phase caption at the top centre that changes with the phase. No title inside the canvas (the card has one). Use plain sans-serif labels.

spec.title: Run the trunk once, the denoiser many times
spec.caption: The trunk (Pairformer with recycling) runs once to produce the conditioning c = (s, z). The denoiser D_θ(x, σ | c) then reads c at every one of its 200 steps, turning noise at σ = 2560 Å into a 25-point chain. Five samples are drawn in parallel from the same c, so the trunk cost is paid once and the denoiser cost grows with the number of samples.
